question.worked_solution:
The laws of logarithms are:

- ${log}_{n}⁡(a)+{log}_{n}⁡(b)={log}_{n}⁡(ab)$ - the product rule

- ${log}_{n}⁡(a)-{log}_{n}⁡(b)={log}_{n}⁡(\frac{a}{b})$ - the quotient rule

- ${log}_{n}⁡({c}^{m})=m{log}_{n}⁡(c)$ - the power rule

Using the quotient rule and then the power rule for logarithms, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{3y}{\sqrt{x}}) & =\operatorname{log}⁡(3y)-\operatorname{log}⁡(\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{log}⁡(3y)-\operatorname{log}⁡({x}^{1/2}) \\  & =\operatorname{log}⁡(3y)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{log}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$
